title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts & API Examples - Ops and Canonical Fixes
author: Ava Nguyen
content:
Overview

This page documents the operating procedure for Developer Experience documentation focused on SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, and the canonical fixes for the top support issues we see from customers and internal teams. The intent is to provide a single, reproducible workflow for producing, reviewing, publishing, and maintaining developer-facing artifacts used by Redwood product and platform teams.

Scope

- SDK reference guides (Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Go)
- Quickstarts and repo templates (starter projects, infra-as-code snippets)
- API examples (REST and SDK snippets used in docs and sample apps)
- Docs site operating procedures: CI, linting, release cadence, and rollback
- Top support issues and canonical fixes, maintained as a living list for triage and engineering work prioritization

Owner and Audience

- Primary owner: Developer Experience (Engineering)
- Secondary owners: Platform, Serving Runtime, SRE, Product Marketing
- Audience: SDK consumers (engineers/ML engineers), solutions engineers, support engineers, and documentation maintainers

Standards and Conventions

- Language-first: every SDK guide must include a one-page quickstart in Python and JavaScript at minimum. Additional languages require a business case and owner.
- Template naming: kebab-case, short, descriptive (e.g., rlhf-starter-template, embed-search-quickstart).
- Example TTL: all runnable examples must work with the latest public Redwood API + a documented pin for the model and runtime that was used for testing.
- Code formatting: Prettier for JS/TS, black for Python, gofmt for Go. CI enforces linting and formatting.

Docs Site Operating Procedures

1. Branching and PRs
   1. All docs changes are made against the docs-main branch.
   2. Use the docs/<area>/<short-desc> branch naming convention.
   3. PRs require: one content reviewer (DevEx), one technical reviewer (owner team), and passing docsite CI.

2. CI and Tests
   - docsite CI runs: link-checker, markdownlint, code-snippet smoke tests, live example smoke tests (where possible), and accessibility checks (axe).
   - Example smoke tests run against a sandbox API key and must complete within 30s on CI.
   - Failure modes: broken links and failing snippets block merge; minor style failures produce warnings but do not block.

3. Release cadence
   - Minor content updates: merge to docs-main and deploy automatically to staging; nightly promotion to prod unless blocked.
   - Major guides or structural changes: schedule a docs release with release notes and a coordinated announcement.

4. Rollback and Emergency Fixes
   - For critical regressions (broken quickstarts, API sample that exposes secrets, major broken links): tag an emergency docs patch, open a hotfix PR, and push to production after expedited review (DevEx + on-call owner).

SDK Guides: Structure and Required Sections

Every SDK guide must include the following sections in this canonical order:

- Title and short summary (1-2 lines)
- Prerequisites (SDK version, runtime, credentials, minimum model)
- Installation (CLI and package manager commands)
- Minimal quickstart (copy-paste runnable in <= 10 lines)
- Common usage patterns and configuration (batching, streaming, KV cache usage, auth)
- Error handling and retry guidance (SLO-aware retry recommendations)
- Troubleshooting (links to support KB entries)
- Change log / version compatibility notes

Template catalog (example table)

| Template | Path | Owner Team | Supported Languages | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| embed-search-quickstart | /templates/embed-search | developer-experience | Python, JS | Includes Dockerfile and sample data generator |
| realtime-chat-starter | /templates/realtime-chat | eng-platform | JS/TS | Websocket-based streaming and function calling demo |
| dedicated-deploy-iac | /templates/dedicated-iac | eng-infra | Terraform | Reference architecture for Dedicated deployment |

Quickstarts and Templates: Best Practices

- Keep quickstarts under 200 LOC. Focus on one small value prop (e.g., embeddings-based search).
- Include a README with setup steps and expected outputs and a demo GIF or short screencast link.
- Tag templates with metadata (supported SDK versions, CI smoke test status, last-tested date).
- Use feature flags for experimental examples and clearly mark them.

API Examples (canonical snippets)

- Canonical examples must exist for: generate/text, chat, embeddings, rerank, streaming responses, and function/tool calling.
- Each example must have: language variants (Python, JS), expected input and output, and a short explanation of when to use the pattern.

Example: Minimal Python text generation quickstart

```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")
resp = client.text.generate(model="redwood-1.0", prompt="Translate to French: 'Hello world'", max_tokens=60)
print(resp.text)
```

Example: JavaScript streaming (Node.js) snippet

```js
import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const stream = client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-chat-1.0', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Summarize the last 2 messages' }] });
for await (const chunk of stream) { process.stdout.write(chunk.delta); }
```

Top Support Issues and Canonical Fixes (living list)

1) Issue: Quickstarts fail for first-time users due to missing environment variables
   - Symptom: Examples raise authentication errors or 401 responses in CI / local runs.
   - Root cause: Samples assume REDWOOD_API_KEY is set; onboarding checklist omitted.
   - Canonical fix: Update all quickstarts to include a preamble with export examples and add a local.env.sample file. CI adds a check that an example run includes the expected 200/201 response.

2) Issue: Streaming examples hang on older Node versions
   - Symptom: Streams never yield final token on Node <= 16.
   - Root cause: use of native async iterator with runtime polyfill mismatch.
   - Canonical fix: update sample code to include a note on Node >= 18 and add a small compatibility wrapper in the examples repo.

3) Issue: Embeddings demo produces low-quality results after model upgrade
   - Symptom: Search relevance regression reported in QA.
   - Root cause: model upgrade (unpinned) changed embedding dimensionality and default normalization.
   - Canonical fix: pin embedding model in the quickstart, add a migration guide for customers, and include a code snippet that normalizes vectors.

4) Issue: Dedicated deployment template network misconfiguration
   - Symptom: Customers cannot reach private endpoints after applying the terraform module.
   - Root cause: Example subnet cidr overlap with default VPC; missing explicit route table attachment in template.
   - Canonical fix: Update the template with explicit VPC/subnet examples, add validation scripts, and update the troubleshooting section in the template README.

5) Issue: API example uses deprecated parameter names
   - Symptom: Confusing 400 errors with "unknown parameter" during example runs.
   - Root cause: docs were not updated after an API rename.
   - Canonical fix: Add a docs linter that checks examples against a small schema generator and add a regression test to block mismatched params.

Triage and Escalation Process for New Support Issues

1. New support issue logged -> Documentation Triage board (DevEx owner) within 24 hours.
2. Triage adds severity, reproducer steps, and assigns to owner team.
3. For severity >= P1 (broken quickstart, leaking secrets, or security-relevant): create a hotfix PR and tag the on-call SRE + DevEx lead.
4. For P2/P3: schedule in the next Docs sprint with an ETA.

Maintaining the Canonical Examples Repository

- Repository: github.com/redwood-inference/devex-examples (owner: developer-experience)
- CI: nightly smoke tests against a sandbox key; weekly dependency updates via renovate; monthly manual review for UX/clarity.
- Labeling: use labels example-status: smoke-passing | smoke-failing | needs-review.

Metrics and SLAs for Docs Reliability

- Target: < 1 critical broken example shipped to prod per quarter.
- CI coverage: 90% of canonical examples have a smoke test in CI.
- Time-to-fix: P1 docs regressions fixed within 24 hours; P2 within 7 days.

Onboarding Checklist for New Examples

1. Create example PR against devex-examples with README and smoke test.
2. Add metadata file: template-metadata.yaml (fields: name, owner_team, last_tested, sdk_versions).
3. Add unit / smoke test in .github/workflows/example-smoke.yml.
4. Request review from DevEx and owner team.
5. Merge and monitor nightly CI for 48 hours.

Appendix: Example template-metadata.yaml (format)

name: embed-search-quickstart
owner_team: developer-experience
last_tested: 2026-07-10
sdk_versions: [python:3.11, node:18]
